newsitem.title: CHINA: China provinces shuts illegal futures firms.
newsitem.headline: China provinces shuts illegal futures firms.

text.p: Authorities in China's northwestern Gansu and southern Jiangxi provinces have closed 11 firms found trading illegal financial futures, the Securities Daily said on Thursday.
In northwestern Gansu, central bank officials had teamed up with officials of the Public Security Bureau to combat a rise in illegal futures deals, the newspaper said.

They closed 10 firms in the province, mainly in the provincial capital, Lanzhou, that were found trading unauthorised futures contracts, it said. Most were trading financial futures related to Hong Kong's Hang Seng index.
The illegal futures trading had disrupted financial order, it said.
Officials had seized 697 dealing machines and frozen a total of 1.34 million yuan ($161,445) in illegal funds, the newspaper said. It did not identify the firms and gave no other details.
In Jiangxi, officials in Jiujiang city had ordered the Long Tai Investment and Development Co to halt its illegal futures business and frozen its bank deposits, the newspaper said.
The firm was also found trading financial futures contracts based on the Hang Seng index, it said, but gave no details.
